ABC Fund: More Than Market Beta

Peer performance insights for the 2027 conference

Kieron Maseko (26572982)

November 2026

1 The case for ABC Fund in three points

  • Most active managers mostly deliver market beta. The typical peer has a beta of 0.83, and the market explains 85% of its returns.
  • ABC Fund is genuinely different. Its beta is now 0.4, lower than 2% of peers, and its returns follow its own decisions rather than the industry consensus.
  • The difference has paid off. Since 2015 ABC has beaten both the typical peer and the benchmark, with less volatility, and it protects capital best when markets fall.

6 Where the edge comes from: falling markets

7 Does high market dispersion reward ABC?

8 Dispersion: what we can and cannot say

  • Over a year or more, the claim holds. In the most dispersed 12-month periods ABC beat the typical peer by 9.6%, against 2% in other periods.
  • Month to month, it does not. In the single most dispersed months ABC actually lagged its peers (it beat them in only 38% of those months).
  • Most of the evidence comes from one period (2020-2022). We suggest presenting dispersion as supporting colour, and leading with ABC’s low beta and downside protection.

9 Why ABC belongs in client portfolios

  • Something other than market beta: clients can buy beta cheaply in an index fund; ABC offers a different return stream.
  • A better ride: higher returns than the typical peer and the benchmark since 2015, with less volatility.
  • Protection when it matters: ABC has done best when markets fall, which is when clients need it most.
  • Caveats: past performance does not guarantee future returns; the analysis uses returns only and covers 2015-2025, and ABC tends to lag in strong rising markets.
